channel.title: UT-REAL’s Blog
channel.description: Scaling and Validating AI-Enabled Simulation Assessment Across University of Texas Medical Schools

item.title: Wayfinder: Upload Encounters and Run Automated Grading in MAPLES
item.description: Watch Minhan Park and Licheng Yi demonstrate Wayfinder beyond rubric authoring: upload an encounter with media, create a group, start a grading run, check status, and summarize results from chat.

item.title: Wayfinder: AI-Assisted Rubric Authoring in MAPLES
item.description: Watch Minhan Park and Licheng Yi demonstrate Wayfinder: create a structured rubric from a short description, enhance it with accept/reject suggestions, transform it for a new scenario, and continue in chat.

item.title: Reimagining OSCE Grading and Medical Education at UT Southwestern
item.description: On Healthcare AI Pioneers, Thomas Dalton and Andrew Jamieson discuss UT Southwestern’s AI-enabled OSCE assessment work: rubrics, multimodal evidence, staged rollout, human review, and precision education.

item.title: MAPLES Walkthrough: From Rubric Upload to Faculty Review
item.description: Watch Ameer Hamza Shakur walk through the MAPLES workflow: upload a rubric, group OSCE encounters, run AI-assisted grading, review cited evidence, and export validated results.

item.title: Project MAPLES Holds All-Site Kickoff
item.description: Participating UT medical school partners met to launch the UT REAL-funded MAPLES project and begin phased deployment planning.

item.title: Award Setup Complete — Partner Site Planning Begins
item.description: With award setup materials submitted and infrastructure partnerships forming, the UT-REAL consortium transitions from setup to active Phase 1 planning.

item.title: UTSW Pilot Surpasses 7,000 AI-Graded Encounters
item.description: The lead site reaches a major milestone with over 7,000 standardized patient encounters graded using AI in production, establishing the foundation for multi-site expansion.

item.title: Project Funded by UT REAL Health AI Pilot Program
item.description: Our project receives $300,000 from the UT System UT REAL Health AI Pilot Program to scale AI-powered simulation assessment across six UT medical schools over 18 months.
